summary: A cavity-mediated architecture uses tunable qubit-cavity couplers to enable dynamically reconfigurable interactions between arbitrary superconducting qubit pairs through a shared bus resonator, achieving iSWAP and CZ gates in 45–70 ns with coherent errors below $10^{-4}$ and residual $ZZ$ interactions suppressed to kilohertz levels. Simulations of a four-qubit system demonstrate selective non-local two-qubit gates for all qubit pairs with fidelities exceeding 99.9% and minimal spectator crosstalk, relaxing geometric constraints on qubit placement.
motivation: Superconducting quantum processors with nearest-neighbor-only connectivity require swap networks that increase circuit depth and accumulated error; extending connectivity to arbitrary qubit pairs without direct coupling enables higher error-correction encoding rates and native long-range-interacting simulations.
method: The architecture uses frequency-tunable transmon couplers mediating interactions between qubits and a shared $\lambda/2$ coplanar waveguide resonator at $\omega_R/2\pi = 3.85$ GHz. Qubits park at 4–5 GHz and couplers at 6–7 GHz in the idle state; lowering selected couplers to $\sim 4.3$ GHz activates cavity-mediated exchange coupling $2g_{QQ}/2\pi \approx 25$ MHz between chosen pairs while others remain isolated. iSWAP and CZ gates use Slepian-like frequency trajectories with polynomial shaping, optimized numerically through diagonalization of the full circuit Hamiltonian including capacitive couplings $(C_{QC}, C_{QR}, C_{CR}) = (3.7, 1.0, 37.4)$ fF and anharmonicities $(\alpha_Q/2\pi, \alpha_C/2\pi) = -(220, 268)$ MHz.
result: Two-qubit simulations achieve iSWAP fidelity 99.995% at $t_g = 45$ ns and CZ fidelity 99.998% at $t_g = 58$ ns with coherent errors $< 10^{-5}$; four-qubit simulations show all six qubit-pair iSWAP gates at $>99.91\%$ fidelity and CZ gates at $>99.91\%$ fidelity with $\varepsilon_{ZZ} < 2 \times 10^{-4}$ on spectators. For realistic $T_1, T_\phi \sim 100$ µs, total gate fidelity exceeds 99.9%; at $T_1, T_\phi \sim 300$ µs the four-qubit CZ fidelity approaches 99.9%.
